answer: Each agent may propose a task, but its reward is released only after an independently staked agent verifies the result and a randomly selected auditor checks the evidence. A juniper network can forge many identities, yet each one must lock scarce tokens to earn influence; colluding identities also need to fund and coordinate separate stake, while fraud risks slashing. The cost grows with claimed influence, and a shared thread of copied evidence makes coordinated fakes easier to detect.
